label: Juju dhau
note: Newar sweet curd from Bhaktapur, Nepal: milk and brown sugar, set in clay pots

about.text: Juju dhau, 'king of yoghurt' in Nepal Bhasa, is a thick, custard-like sweet curd from Bhaktapur, made by the Newar from boiled, sweetened buffalo milk and set in clay pots.

how.text: The milk is poured into the pots in batches, each after a boil, and the starter is added while it is still warm; the husks keep it warm until it sets.

steps.note: Buffalo milk is boiled, in batches, a 60 L boil taking about half an hour.

steps.name: sweeten
steps.note: Brown sugar is stirred in once the milk boils.

adds.vessel: unglazed clay pot (kataro) with a clay lid, standing on rice husks and wrapped in warm cloth

steps.note: Two to three spoons of plain curd (backslopped) go into each pot while the milk is still warm.

processing.text: Two to three spoons of plain curd go into each pot; species are not given.
